prompts.display_text: Pin a South American country with a dedicated temple.
prompts.text_original: Pin a South American country with at least one dedicated temple (as of October 2026).
prompts.note: Only Guyana and Suriname lack one.
prompts.summary: South America's first temple was dedicated in Sao Paulo, Brazil, in 1978. By 2002 ten South American countries had one, the last of them Asuncion, Paraguay. As of October 2026, only Guyana and Suriname lack a temple.

prompts.display_text: Pin a Central American or Caribbean country or territory, not Mexico, with a dedicated temple.
prompts.text_original: Excluding Mexico, pin a Central American or Caribbean country or territory with a dedicated temple (as of October 2026).
prompts.summary: Guatemala City got the first temple in Central America in 1984, and Guatemala now has four. Costa Rica and the Dominican Republic followed in 2000, and more have come since, most recently Port-au-Prince (2019), San Juan (2023) and Managua (2026).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where an Indigenous American language with Book of Mormon text is spoken natively.
prompts.text_original: A country where an Indigenous American language with Book of Mormon text (Aymara, Quechua, Mayan languages, Navajo, Kuna, Guarani...) is spoken natively
prompts.summary: Since 1977 Book of Mormon text has come out in many Indigenous languages of the Americas. Guatemala has Cakchiquel, Kekchi, Quiche and Mam; Bolivia has Aymara and Quechua; Paraguay has Guarani; and in the United States, Navajo has had selections since 1980.

answers.name: Guatemala
answers.fact: Cakchiquel, Kekchi, Quiche and Mam all got Book of Mormon text from 1978 to 1983.

answers.name: Bolivia
answers.fact: Aymara and Bolivian Quechua have Book of Mormon text.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: Maya (1983) and Tzotzil (1992) selections serve Mexico's south.

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: Peruvian Quechua selections came in 1979; Aymara is also spoken there.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: Navajo selections came in 1980, with a revised edition in 1998.

answers.name: Ecuador
answers.fact: Ecuadorian Quichua selections came in 1980 and the full text in 2011.

answers.name: Paraguay
answers.fact: Guarani selections came in 1982 and the full text in 2009.

answers.name: Argentina
answers.fact: Guarani, with a full 2009 Book of Mormon, is spoken in northeast Argentina.

answers.name: Belize
answers.fact: Kekchi (Q'eqchi'), with Book of Mormon text, is spoken in southern Belize; Yucatec Maya is also spoken in Belize.

answers.name: Chile
answers.fact: Aymara, with a full 1986 Book of Mormon, is spoken in far northern Chile.

answers.name: Colombia
answers.fact: Kuna (Guna), with Book of Mormon selections, is spoken natively by the Guna of northwest Colombia.

prompts.display_text: Pin a Central American or Caribbean country or territory, not Mexico, with 25,000+ Church members (end of 2025).
prompts.text_original: Pin a Central American (Guatemala to Panama) or Caribbean country or territory with 25,000 or more Church members (end of 2025).
prompts.note: Next below the line: Jamaica (about 7,900), Belize (about 5,700).
prompts.summary: Guatemala had about 297,000 Church members at the end of 2025, the most in Central America and the Caribbean. Honduras, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador and Nicaragua each had more than 100,000, and Panama, Costa Rica, Haiti and Puerto Rico had 25,000 or more.

answers.name: Puerto Rico
answers.fact: About 27,000 members, just over the line.

prompts.display_text: Pin a European country whose official language first got the Book of Mormon from 1997 to 2021.
prompts.text_original: A European country where an official language first got the Book of Mormon between 1997 and 2021
prompts.summary: Between 1997 and 2021 the Book of Mormon reached many languages of eastern and southern Europe, starting with Ukrainian (1997) and Albanian (1999). Estonian, Latvian and Lithuanian all came in 2000, followed by Slovenian (2002), Serbian (2008) and Slovak (2013).

answers.name: Ukraine
answers.fact: The Ukrainian Book of Mormon appeared in 1997.

answers.name: Albania
answers.fact: The Albanian Book of Mormon appeared in 1999.

answers.name: Estonia
answers.fact: The Estonian Book of Mormon appeared in 2000.

answers.name: Lithuania
answers.fact: The Lithuanian Book of Mormon appeared in 2000.

answers.name: Latvia
answers.fact: The Latvian Book of Mormon appeared in 2000.

answers.name: Serbia
answers.fact: The Serbian Book of Mormon appeared in 2008.

answers.name: Slovakia
answers.fact: The Slovak Book of Mormon appeared in 2013, eighty years after Czech.

answers.name: Slovenia
answers.fact: The Slovenian Book of Mormon appeared in 2002.

answers.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
answers.fact: Serbian, translated 2008, is one of Bosnia's official languages.

answers.name: North Macedonia
answers.fact: The full Macedonian Book of Mormon appeared in 2023; Albanian (1999) is also co-official there.

answers.name: Kosovo
answers.fact: Albanian (1999) and Serbian (2008) are both official in Kosovo.
